title: Be a Zookeeper
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for Shellfie.

pages: Today, you are a zookeeper! You take care of animals at the zoo.
You wear a uniform with a shirt, shorts or pants, a hat, gloves, and strong boots.
First, you make breakfast for the animals. The giraffes get leaves and hay, the penguins get fish, and the gorillas get fruit and vegetables.
Next, you clean the animals' homes. There is a lot of poop to scoop. Hold your nose!
You lean over the fence to give the giraffe her leaves. She licks your hat right off your head!
The sea lion splashes you with a big wave. Now you are wet from your hat to your boots.
You give the animals puzzles and toys, like a ball with treats inside. This keeps their brains busy.
You watch each animal closely. Is it eating? Is it moving well? If something seems wrong, you call the zoo vet.
You work with a team: other keepers, vets, people who plan the animals' meals, and teachers who tell visitors about animals.
The best part? You get to know each animal, and the animals get to know you.
The hardest part? Animals need care every day, even on holidays and in rain or snow.
How do you become a zookeeper? Most zookeepers go to college for about 4 years to study animals or biology. Many also volunteer or train at a zoo.
What can you do now? Visit a zoo. Watch the birds and bugs in your yard and draw them in a nature journal. Look for zoo camps for kids.
